report.summary: Login failures and missing OTPs were caused by a third-party outage at otp-provider starting at 13:40 UTC, which returned 503 Service Unavailable errors and elevated latency, cascading into auth-service and mobile-bff error rate spikes.

supporting.note: otp-provider error rate spiked starting at 13:40 UTC, reaching a peak of 80.04%.
otp-provider p99 latency increased starting at 13:40 UTC, peaking at ~5.5s.
Shows auth-service receiving 503 Service Unavailable errors from otp-provider starting at 13:40.
Auth-service error rate sharply spiked starting at 13:40.
Mobile-bff error rate spiked immediately after at 13:41 due to dependency on auth-service.
A deployment occurred on auth-service shortly before the incident window at 13:05.
Users hit OTP resend limits starting at 13:42, which relates directly to the feature introduced in chg-9363.

contradicting.note: otp-provider error rate spiked independently at 13:40, indicating provider-side failure rather than a client-triggered issue.
otp-provider latency degraded significantly starting at 13:40.
Explicit 503 Service Unavailable responses indicate server-side vendor unavailability.

facts.text: auth-service error rate metric spiked starting at 2026-10-13T13:40:00+00:00, reaching a peak of 39.06% error rate.
mobile-bff error rate metric spiked starting at 2026-10-13T13:41:00+00:00, reaching 5.36% error rate.
notification-service showed no error rate or latency anomaly during the incident window.
auth-service logs show frequent 503 Service Unavailable errors from otp-provider beginning at 2026-10-13T13:40:13+00:00.
auth-service users hit OTP resend limits starting at 2026-10-13T13:42:35+00:00 due to upstream delivery failures.
auth-service was deployed at 2026-10-13T13:05:00+00:00 (chg-9363) with summary 'auth-service v7.1.3: limit OTP resends to 3 per 10 minutes'.
otp-provider error rate spiked starting at 13:40 UTC, reaching a peak of 80.04% at 13:52 UTC.
otp-provider p99 latency increased starting at 13:40 UTC, reaching a peak of 5495.16 ms at 13:56 UTC.
otp-provider request rate (rps) remained normal without any anomaly during the incident window.

assumptions: The root cause of otp-provider's degradation is internal to the third-party vendor's infrastructure, as request rates (rps) remained normal.

timeline.event: auth-service was deployed with v7.1.3 (limit OTP resends to 3 per 10 minutes)
otp-provider error rate and latency spiked, and auth-service began logging 503 Service Unavailable errors
mobile-bff error rate spiked due to dependency on auth-service
auth-service users hit OTP resend limits due to upstream delivery failures

recommended_actions.action: Coordinate with the external otp-provider vendor to investigate their infrastructure degradation and recovery status.
recommended_actions.rationale: The root cause is an external service degradation at otp-provider starting at 13:40 UTC.

recommended_actions.action: Implement circuit breakers or fallback notification channels in auth-service to gracefully handle third-party OTP provider outages without exhausting user retry limits.
recommended_actions.rationale: Failures from the external provider directly caused auth-service to return 503 errors and users to hit resend limits.

recommended_actions.action: Establish secondary redundant OTP providers for automatic failover during third-party outages.
recommended_actions.rationale: Single dependency on otp-provider caused a direct service outage impacting a third of all logins.
